# Proposal: Fractional AI Governance Advisor

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Fractional AI Governance Advisor, AI Governance Academy
**Source:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026
**Decision expected:** 15 December 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It has about 1,100 staff and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, with headquarters in the Netherlands. Its AI use is at the piloting stage:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

The Client has not completed a prior Academy program, so there are no carried-forward open items.

**Regulatory drivers.** The Client names the EU AI Act and GDPR.

**Audit finding.** An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems.

**Certification target.** The Client intends to begin ISO/IEC 42001 work next year. The start date is not fixed and is rendered `Unknown`.

**Incumbent frameworks.** The Profile Block lists an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and an ISO 9001 quality management system. This proposal does not assume these frameworks contain any AI-relevant register, process, control or record. Their reusable content is `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake.

**Stated objective.** The Sponsor's objective is direct: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

**Stated constraints.** Customer data must stay in the EU. The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff. Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

## 2. The Case for Continuous Fractional Advisory at This Stage

At the piloting stage, governance decisions are made alongside technical and operational decisions rather than after them. Three conditions favor continuous advisory over a one-time assessment:

1. **A dated objective.** The Client has a stated production target for visual inspection in Q2 2027.
2. **A documented gap.** The internal audit finding on the AI system inventory needs a response.
3. **A pipeline of use cases.** A forecasting use case is planned, so new systems will need intake and review.

A standing advisor helps the executive team sequence these demands, keep artifacts current as pilots change and prepare for ISO/IEC 42001 work without overbuilding ahead of need.

The engagement is guided by three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. Accountability for every AI decision remains with named Tamarack Instruments personnel. The advisor informs those decisions and does not take them.

The engagement draws on two open frameworks: the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) is available as a reference if board-level reporting is requested.

## 3. Annual Arc

The arc is sequenced by engagement quarter. The engagement start date is `Unknown` and depends on the 15 December 2026 decision. If the start falls in January 2027, the Q2 2027 production target lands within engagement Quarter 2. A later start would compress Quarters 1 and 2, and the plan would be adjusted at intake.

**Quarter 1: Stabilize**
- Respond to the internal audit finding by establishing an AI system inventory covering the deployed chatbot, the visual inspection pilot and the planned forecasting use case.
- Define governance roles and decision rights. Who owns each system and each artifact is `Unknown` and will be designated by the Client.
- Prepare questions on EU AI Act classification and GDPR obligations for each use case, routed to external counsel for determination.
- Confirm with the Client whether the visual inspection system touches production staff. This determines when works council consultation is required. Its status is `Unknown`.
- Confirm how the EU customer data residency constraint applies to each use case. Current data flows are `Unknown`.

**Quarter 2: Deepen and Prepare for Production**
- Build a pre-production governance gate for visual inspection. The gate covers risk assessment, human oversight design, monitoring and evidence of works council consultation where the Client determines it applies.
- Support executive decision-making on go-live readiness against the Q2 2027 target.
- Map which content from the incumbent ISMS and quality management system can be reused for AI governance, based on what intake confirms exists.

**Quarter 3: Assure**
- Conduct an ISO/IEC 42001 readiness gap assessment, timed to the Client's chosen start date. That date remains `Unknown`.
- Design evidence collection practices and the internal audit approach for AI controls. The internal audit team's role in this is to be agreed with the Client.
- Review post-production monitoring for visual inspection.

**Quarter 4: Evolve**
- Run the planned sales forecasting use case through the intake and risk process established in Quarter 1.
- Set the forward ISO/IEC 42001 preparation plan.
- Prepare a year-in-review assessment and a renewal options memo.

All ISO/IEC 42001 work is framed as readiness. No certification or audit outcome is promised.

## 4. Cadence and Access Model

| Element | Frequency | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Executive advisory session | Monthly | Decisions, risks and priorities with the Sponsor and designated executives |
| Working session with the governance team | Monthly | Artifact development and implementation guidance |
| Asynchronous availability | Ongoing, for defined question categories | Timely guidance between sessions |
| Quarterly governance review | Quarterly | Progress, artifact maturity and the next quarter plan |

Attendees for each session are `Unknown` and will be designated by the Sponsor. The audience roles listed in discovery are the General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. Question categories and response windows will be defined at intake.

## 5. Scope

**In scope:** governance evolution, implementation guidance, audit preparation, AI strategy and executive decision support.

**Out of scope:** legal advice, certification body functions, staff augmentation and incident command.

The advisor is not counsel of record. Legal questions, including EU AI Act and GDPR interpretation, route to external counsel. Regulatory developments raised during the engagement are flagged for counsel verification and are not presented as settled advice.

## 6. Investment

The engagement runs for 12 months, renewable, at US$10,000 per month, for a total of US$120,000 over the term.

The Client has approved a budget of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. How the engagement maps to that budget depends on the Client's fiscal year boundaries and the engagement start date, both `Unknown`. The amount required in the following fiscal year depends on the same factors. We recommend confirming both before the 15 December 2026 decision so that funding for the full term is clear.
